title: One compatible descending step at finitely many localizations
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a cochain complex of $A$-modules, $f_j$ a finite family of ring elements, and $b,n\in\mathbb Z$ with $n\le b+1$. Fix derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] over $A_{f_j}$ and suppose $Q(M_{f_j})$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] for every $j$. Let $\alpha:F\to M$ be a chain map, with $F^i=0$ for $i<n$ and $i>b$, and every $F^i$ a finitely generated free $A$-module. Suppose $H^i(\alpha_{f_j})$ is invertible for $i>n$ and surjective for $i=n$. There are $G$, $\beta:G\to M$, and $\tau:F\to G$, such that $G^i=0$ for $i<n-1$ and $i>b$, every $G^i$ is finite free, $H^i(\beta_{f_j})$ is invertible for $i>n-1$ and surjective for $i=n-1$, $\tau\beta=\alpha$, and $\tau^i$ is invertible for $i\ge n$. Neither a unit-ideal condition on the family nor global cohomology vanishing is required.

proof.text: At each localization use the long exact sequence of the cone to show zero cone homology in every degree at least n: the homology map at i is epic and at i+1 is monic. The scalar extension of F is bounded finite free. Use pseudo-coherence iff all m-approximations for localized M at n-1, then cone pseudo-coherence at n-1 and finite top cohomology to show finite cone homology in degree n-1. The additive cone comparison identifies this with homology of the scalar-extended global cone.

Flatness of localization and the homology comparison identify localized cone homology with scalar extension of global cone homology. Apply simultaneous finite scalar surjections to global degree-(n-1) cone homology. This supplies a finite free P and a map p to that homology whose scalar extensions are epic. Lift p through the epic homology projection from global cone cycles using projectivity of P. The lift q followed by the homology projection is p, so each scalar extension of q followed by the projection is epic. No denominators need to be cleared in cycle representatives.

Apply the fully proved cone-cycle attachment for a family of additive epi-preserving functors, using scalar extension as the family. It constructs G, beta and tau, retaining the old terms, preserving the upper and finite free bounds, and making every scalar extension of new cone homology vanish in degrees at least n-1. Flatness identifies these images with homology of the localized new cones. Their long exact sequences give isomorphisms for localized beta above n-1 and epimorphisms at n-1. The attachment supplies tau beta = alpha and invertible tau components for i>=n.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_localization_free_step (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) [∀ j : Fin r, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.Away (f j)))] (hlocal : ∀ j : Fin r, IsPseudoCoherent (Q.obj ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M))) (b n : ℤ) (hn : n ≤ b + 1) (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (α : F ⟶ M) (hupper : F.IsStrictlyLE b) (hlower : F.IsStrictlyGE n) (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free A (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (F.X i)) (hiso : ∀ j : Fin r, ∀ i : ℤ, n < i → QuasiIsoAt ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) i) (hepi : ∀ j : Fin r, Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α) n)) : ∃ (G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (β : G ⟶ M), G.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ G.IsStrictlyGE (n - 1) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free A (G.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (G.X i)) ∧ (∀ j : Fin r, ∀ i : ℤ, n - 1 < i → QuasiIsoAt ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map β) i) ∧ (∀ j : Fin r, Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map β) (n - 1))) ∧ ∃ τ : F ⟶ G, τ ≫ β = α ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i → IsIso (τ.f i)
